service_record.event_desc.germany.rank.u: New to the line, you fly tight on a leader’s wing and learn fast or die fast. Your logbook fills one sortie at a time.
service_record.event_desc.germany.rank.f: You’ve seen flak and fighters up close and you don’t flinch. Men follow your turns because they’ve learned you bring them home.
service_record.event_desc.germany.rank.o: Veteran hands, tired eyes—still climbing into the cockpit. You lead by example and the rookies copy everything you do.
service_record.event_desc.germany.rank.l: Now you carry a commission and the weight that comes with it. You still fly the same sky, just with more eyes depending on you.
service_record.event_desc.germany.rank.o: You lead flights into weather, flak, and bad odds. The Staffel watches how you handle the first burst and the last decision.
service_record.event_desc.germany.rank.h: Command and combat collide: paperwork at dawn, engine heat by noon. You fly when it matters and your name rides every outcome.
service_record.event_desc.germany.rank.m: Your map table is larger than your cockpit time now. When you do fly, it’s because the mission can’t afford mistakes.
service_record.event_desc.germany.rank.o: You keep the unit running and the losses bear your signature. You fly rarely—usually to see the front with your own eyes.
A commander with a pilot’s past and a war on his desk. If you take off, it’s for a reason everyone remembers.
service_record.event_desc.germany.rank.g: You move squadrons like chess pieces and count fuel like blood. Flight time is rare; responsibility is constant.
The war looks different from this altitude—briefings, orders, consequences. You earned wings once; now you carry a theater.
You’ve earned the right to wear wings—and to be sent back up tomorrow. Training is over; the war starts now.
A first hard mark of combat service. Not glory—just proof you were there when it counted.
You didn’t just survive; you delivered results. The unit knows you’re the one to call when it’s hot.
A Luftwaffe trophy for men who fly beyond “enough.” It’s handed to those who keep coming back with victories and scars.
Sustained combat success, the long grind turned into metal. You’ve been tested—repeatedly—and held.
The kind of award that changes how people look at you. Fame is loud; the war is louder.
More proof, more pressure. They expect miracles now—and they write your name in bigger letters.
A mark for relentless frontline achievement. You’re not just fighting—you’re shaping the fight.
Rare, heavy, and impossible to ignore. Your record is legend; your risk stays real.
The top shelf, almost unheard of. You’ve become a symbol—and symbols still bleed.
You’ve logged enough combat sorties to know the routine is deadly. The front doesn’t care how brave you feel.
A long run of sorties under pressure. You’ve outlasted luck and learned discipline.
Heavy operational time at the sharp end. You’ve lived where the sky is full of fire.
An extreme tally of frontline sorties. You’ve been to war so often it feels like home—and that’s the danger.
First blood paid to the front. You came back—this time.
More wounds, fewer illusions. You’re still flying, but you’ve started counting what it costs.
You’ve been hit again and again and kept returning. The badge shines; the damage doesn’t.
service_record.event_desc.britain.rank.s: Fresh wings, cold cockpit, and the Channel wind cutting through everything. Stay with your leader and keep your eyes moving.
service_record.event_desc.britain.rank.f: You’ve learned the sound of trouble before you see it. In the air, you’re steady—because panic kills.
service_record.event_desc.britain.rank.w: A hard veteran in a soft uniform. You fly like you’ve paid for every lesson—and you have.
service_record.event_desc.britain.rank.p: Commissioned, but still proving yourself every sortie. The squadron judges you by the way you hold formation under fire.
service_record.event_desc.britain.rank.f: You can lead a section and make it stick. When the radio goes quiet, your decisions speak loudest.
You balance duty rosters and deadly skies. You still fly—because you won’t ask men to do what you won’t.
service_record.event_desc.britain.rank.s: The squadron’s tempo is yours to set: push too hard and you break it. You fly when the moment needs a steady hand.
service_record.event_desc.britain.rank.w: You command wings and you feel every loss. You go up sometimes—enough to keep the war honest.
service_record.event_desc.britain.rank.g: A commander with a pilot’s instincts and a strategist’s burden. You fly rarely now, but you never stop listening to the engines.
service_record.event_desc.britain.rank.a: You direct whole air battles from reports and maps. If you fly, it’s exceptional—and everyone notices.
The air war runs through your desk and into the sky. Flight is rare; command is relentless.
Your wings are sewn on, and your life is scheduled around sorties. Welcome to the line.
Your name made it into the official reports. Quiet recognition for work done when it was most dangerous.
Courage and grit from an airman who kept flying. Earned the hard way, one operation after another.
They’re saying you did it again. Same sky, same risk—more proof you don’t quit.
Rare repeat recognition for relentless operations. You’re becoming the kind of flyer the squadron leans on.
Gallantry in the air, the kind that holds a formation together. The ribbon looks clean; the sorties weren’t.
Another round of hard flying that stood out. You’ve made danger a habit—and lived through it.
Almost unheard of. You’ve repeatedly done what shouldn’t be survivable.
Leadership under fire, not just bravery. You kept men fighting when the odds went ugly.
A second time they credit your command in combat. You’ve carried responsibility where it hurts.
Exceptionally rare and hard-won. You’ve led through repeated crisis and come out standing.
The highest kind of courage—beyond orders, beyond reason. A moment that becomes history.
A second VC is almost myth. It means you faced the impossible twice and refused to yield.
Proof the war reached you personally. The body keeps the receipt.
Hit again, still flying. Survival isn’t luck anymore—it’s endurance.
Three wounds and still on the roster. The squadron sees you and knows what it costs.
service_record.event_desc.usa.rank.first: You keep the unit stitched together when the mission tears it apart. If you fly, it’s to share the risk, not the glory.
service_record.event_desc.usa.rank.fligh: You’re rated to fly and thrown into the grinder. Learn fast, hit hard, and don’t waste luck.
service_record.event_desc.usa.rank.chief: You’re the quiet expert—engines, tactics, nerves of steel. When it gets ugly, they want you in the formation.
service_record.event_desc.usa.rank.secon: Brand-new bars, same flak and same fear. Your lead is light, but the war doesn’t care.
service_record.event_desc.usa.rank.first: You’ve seen enough to stop pretending it’s easy. Now you lead flights and carry men through bad weather and worse skies.
service_record.event_desc.usa.rank.capta: You’re a leader and a target both. You still fly—because credibility is earned at altitude.
service_record.event_desc.usa.rank.major: Plans, briefings, and harder calls than trigger pulls. You fly selectively now, usually when the mission needs a proven hand.
service_record.event_desc.usa.rank.lieut: Bigger command, fewer takeoffs. When you do fly, it’s to see the truth beyond the paperwork.
service_record.event_desc.usa.rank.colon: You command from the top but you’ve flown the hard miles. Flight is rare—your war is coordination and consequence.
service_record.event_desc.usa.rank.briga: You shape operations across units and bases. If you take the air, it’s a statement—and a risk you don’t take lightly.
service_record.event_desc.usa.rank.major: Strategy, logistics, and the weight of whole formations. Your flying days are mostly memory, but the sky is still yours.
service_record.event_desc.usa.award.pilo: Your wings say you’re rated and ready. Now the mission board tells you where you’ll bleed for them.
service_record.event_desc.usa.award.air_: Meritorious flying under combat conditions. It’s the war’s way of saying you kept delivering.
You’ve earned it again. Same sky, more missions, more proof.
A steady record of combat flying. You’re becoming a veteran by accumulation.
Repeated awards for repeated sorties. The ribbon stack grows as the risks don’t stop.
service_record.event_desc.usa.award.bron: Combat merit and hard service recognized. Not glamorous—just earned where it’s dangerous.
Another round of meritorious service under fire. They’re counting what you’ve carried.
A third recognition for staying effective in the long grind. You’ve become dependable the hard way.
service_record.event_desc.usa.award.dfc: Heroism or extraordinary achievement in the air. The kind of sortie people talk about afterward.
service_record.event_desc.usa.award.dfc_: You’ve done it again—another exceptional mission, another line in the record.
A sustained pattern of standout flying. The enemy isn’t the only thing watching you now.
Repeated extraordinary performance. Your reputation is built on missions that should’ve gone wrong.
More than most ever see in a lifetime. It means you keep walking into the worst and coming out.
A higher-count mark of repeat awards. You’ve stacked extraordinary sorties like normal work.
service_record.event_desc.usa.award.legi: Outstanding service over time, beyond a single fight. You’ve carried the war on your shoulders and kept it moving.
service_record.event_desc.usa.award.silv: Gallantry in action. A moment of courage that refused to break.
Again, you stood when others might not. Repeated bravery under fire.
A third gallantry award is a hard statement. You don’t just survive trouble—you face it.
service_record.event_desc.usa.award.dsc: Extraordinary heroism in combat. The kind of action that becomes a unit legend.
service_record.event_desc.usa.award.dsc_: A second time for extreme heroism. That’s not luck—that’s a pattern of risk.
A third award for extraordinary heroism. Few ever reach this—and fewer live through it.
Repeated actions at the edge of survivability. Your record reads like a warning label.
Almost unheard of. You’ve done the impossible too many times to count.
service_record.event_desc.usa.award.meda: Valor above and beyond—an act that rewrites what “duty” means. The highest recognition for the darkest moment.
A second Medal of Honor is nearly unimaginable. It means you faced that line twice and crossed it.
service_record.event_desc.usa.award.purp: You were hit by the enemy and paid in blood. The medal is quiet; the memory isn’t.
Wounded again. You carry the damage and keep flying anyway.
Three wounds and still operational. The body keeps score even if the medal does not.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.rank.se: A frontline pilot with little margin and no illusions. You fly, you fight, you hope the engine holds.
You’ve survived enough to teach others how to. The new men watch your hands more than they hear your words.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.rank.ju: You’ve got a commission and a rifleman’s war in the air. Lead tight, strike fast, and don’t linger.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.rank.li: You’re trusted to bring a pair home and still finish the job. The sky is crowded and mercy is scarce.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.rank.se: You lead sorties into flak and weather like it’s routine. Your squadron runs on discipline and stubbornness.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.rank.ca: You command and you still fly hard. The best orders are the ones you’ve tested in your own cockpit.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.rank.ma: You fly less, plan more, and sleep even less. When you do climb out, it’s for missions that must succeed.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.rank.su: Command pulls you away from the line, but you return when it matters. A rare sortie, a familiar smell of fuel and frost.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.rank.co: You carry an air regiment’s fate in your notes and your voice. Flying is occasional; responsibility never is.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.rank.ma: You command formations and watch losses like a ledger of steel. If you fly, it’s exceptional—and never for sport.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.rank.li: The front is vast, the demands endless. You’re a pilot by training, a commander by necessity.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.award.a: You’re marked as aircrew now. The front will use you until the machine or the man breaks.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.award.m: Solid service under fire. You did the work, took the risk, and brought results back.
Personal bravery, close and undeniable. You held your nerve when the sky turned violent.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.award.o: A serious combat award for real results. Not for talk—only for what you did at the front.
They’re recognizing you again. Same war, higher stakes, more proof you’re still delivering.
A third time is no accident. You’ve made a career out of surviving—and winning.
Combat merit that mattered to the Motherland. Earned in the grind, not the parade.
A higher grade for standout performance in battle. Your name is being noticed beyond the regiment.
For leaders who win while outnumbered and under fire. A commander’s award, earned in the air.
Recognition for effective command and successful operations. You made plans work in a world that hates plans.
A major mark of courage and achievement. The kind of ribbon earned only at the sharp end.
They say you’ve done it again. Results repeated, losses endured, mission accomplished.
A third award speaks of a brutal record. You’ve fought hard, long, and successfully.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.award.h: The highest title—heroism carved into the record. It doesn’t make the next sortie easier.
A rare second title for extraordinary repeat heroism. Even comrades look twice when your name is read.
Almost legendary. You’re a symbol now—and symbols are still sent into combat.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.award.o: One of the highest honors, often paired with major heroism. A decoration that carries political weight and frontline respect.
They’re elevating you again for continued distinction. Your war record is becoming impossible to ignore.
A third time is exceptional. It marks a sustained level of achievement few ever reach.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.award.b: A small reward for staying on the roster. The money is nice; the survival is the real prize.
You’ve kept flying while others vanish. The state notices endurance.
A real milestone at the front. You’ve stacked sorties like cordwood and kept moving.
Heavy operational time—hard-earned and rarely clean. You’ve stayed in the fight long enough to be feared.
service_record.event_desc.soviet.award.w: You were wounded and still came back. The stripe is simple; the story isn’t.
Another mark of injury carried forward. You flew hurt, landed alive, and returned to duty.
